audited_by: ep49 render worker (two fresh readers, third reader compared old/new)

faults.what: The one sleeping sea serpent has two closed-eye heads, one stacked under the other, so it reads as two serpents.
faults.where: both heads, left half of the frame

faults.what: The bay holds what reads as two sea creatures where there is one Bakunawa: a finned, flippered whale-serpent at the top and a separate tail coil below.
faults.where: upper third and lower half, left side

faults.what: The red-and-white shop sign right behind Indio's head carries clear pseudo-letters, with a second smaller red sign beside it.
Under the melting star the shapes read as a nose and open lips, the hand holding it has no clear fingers, and a loose sheet of blond hair hangs at the right edge with nobody it belongs to.
faults.where: top of frame under the star, right edge

faults.what: Ma'am Celia is a different woman from shot 28: young, with loose shoulder-length hair and a cream dress, instead of the lined forties woman with red lipstick and a blue-and-white outfit.
Rico is drawn as a spiky-haired teenager in a black jacket with neon patches, not the thirties man in the black-and-red jacket with a camera from shot 39.
The man kneeling to the child wears a plain yellow T-shirt and has a different face and haircut, so he does not read as Rico.
The still has black letterbox bars at the top and bottom (the bottom one about 55 px tall), so it looks like a pasted panel.
Lola's two feet merge into one lump with a row of toes on top, and one leg passes behind a plank it should be in front of; small in the frame.
faults.where: lower right, Lola's feet at the pier edge

faults.what: Rico's jacket is olive with a white T-shirt, not the black-and-red jacket of shot 39; the face itself is close enough.
The grandson Lola asks is a small boy in a red polo, not the forties Indio she is speaking to in the surrounding shots.
A four-armed black clock-hand cross floats in mid-air over the pier with no clock behind it, separate from the stick Indio holds.
Usman has two upright pointed ears and no folded ear.
Usman, seen from behind, has two upright pointed ears and no folded ear.
Usman has both ears folded, not one.
Usman has both ears folded, not one.
Indio is not recognisable: a young brown-haired man in a white open shirt with no grey in his hair, no dark grey coat and no red wrist handkerchief, cut straight after shot 47 where he is on model.
Indio's and M's joined hands are one small fused clump with scribbled fingers.
Indio's hair hangs as a long ponytail with a grey streak down his back instead of a small topknot.
Papa's eyes do not match: one is open, the other half shut and lower.
faults.where: man in black shirt, centre left

faults.what: The engineer's eyes do not match behind her glasses: one is wide open, the other closed in a wink.
The blade has no guard, its dark grip plugs straight into the blade through a gold ferrule, and loose silver blade tips float around it.
faults.where: lower middle and both side edges

faults.what: M's two legs do not match: one is in black trousers and a black shoe, the other is bare with a white ankle sock and strap shoe.
faults.where: lower right, M's legs below the coat

faults.what: The child's lower hand melts into the brown shoulder bag: knuckle lumps and a white cuff are grown into the leather with no readable fingers.
faults.where: child's left side, by the bag

faults.what: The child is a bob-haired girl in a white hoodie and striped shorts here, but a short-haired boy in a blue shirt and green shorts in shot 42.
The close-up hand is muddled: the thumb runs as a long finger split from the wrist and two fingers share one wide stalk behind the clock hub, so the hand reads as boneless at 3x.
The fist at the bottom shows only a thumb and one lump of a curled finger covered in crackle lines like scales, so no fingers can be counted.
faults.where: bottom left, the hand under the tattooed forearm

third_reader.notes: ask_build: red handkerchief on both wrists, plank behind his neck; child_sleeve: the child holds his hand rather than the cuff (minor, not must-fix)
